title: Restricted abelian cohomology admits geometric complex data
statement: Let k:W→S be a morphism, F an abelian etale sheaf on W, q an integer, D:I→Over W a small cofiltered system with affine transitions, and c a cone limiting on underlying schemes. Assume all stage maps to S and the limit map to S are qcqs, and let U→S be affine etale. Define C(A)=H^q(U×_S A, pr_A^* A.hom^*F[0]), and C(f) by canonical derived-adjunction pullback followed by the inverse-image coefficient identification. Let H:Iᵒᵖ→Ab and B be a cocone, with isomorphisms e_i:H_i≅C(D_i) and e₀:B.pt≅C(c.pt). Assume H(f)≫e_j=e_i≫C(D(f)) and B_i≫e₀=e_i≫C(c_i). Then H and B have the geometric complex data of [def-sbc-etale-complex-cohomology-presentation-data]. This comparison assumes the explicit squares; it contains no raw module Hom or scalar-forgetting comparison and asserts no continuity.

source.place: Tags 09Z1 and 0EZM, geometric construction before continuity

proof.text: Construct restrictedOverDiagram, restrictedOverCone and the explicit restrictedOverSingleIso. Pass the underlying scheme limit to Over S using reflection by its forgetful functor. Apply Over.pullback U.hom and Over.forget U.left, which preserve connected limits. Pullback symmetry identifies this limit with the constructed cone. Base change of qcqs morphisms over affine U gives compact and quasi-separated stages; MorphismProperty.pullbackMap gives affine transitions.

Use restrictedOverSingle_coherence for the identity and composition laws and the constant coefficient diagram comparison. All data equalities are reflexive; no data are selected from an existence theorem. The bound is zero by HomologicalComplex.isZero_single_obj_X. The identity cocone of the constant complex is colimiting since I opposite is filtered and hence connected.

Take p=q and P=rawAffineComplexPullback q, whose required canonical expression is reflexivity. The given e and e₀ are the stage and apex comparisons by the definitions of the explicit single complexes. Cancel e_j in the stage square, and expand the inverse cone comparison and identity cocone leg in the apex square. The definitions of restrictedOverSingleIso and restrictedOverCohomologyMap identify the resulting maps. Apply the given he and he₀.

theorem restrictedOverAbelianCocone_complex_data
    {W S : Scheme.{u}} (k : W ⟶ S)
    (F₀ : Sheaf W.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (q : ℤ)
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I] (D₀ : I ⥤ Over W)
    [∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D₀.map f).left]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact ((D₀.obj i).hom ≫ k)]
    [∀ i, QuasiSeparated ((D₀.obj i).hom ≫ k)]
    (c₀ : Cone D₀) (hc₀ : IsLimit ((Over.forget W).mapCone c₀))
    [QuasiCompact (c₀.pt.hom ≫ k)] [QuasiSeparated (c₀.pt.hom ≫ k)]
    (U : S.Etale) [IsAffine U.left]
    (H : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (B : Cocone H)
    (e : ∀ i : I, H.obj (op i) ≅ restrictedOverCohomology k F₀ q (D₀.obj i) U)
    (e₀ : B.pt ≅ restrictedOverCohomology k F₀ q c₀.pt U)
    (he : ∀ (i j : I) (f : j ⟶ i), H.map f.op ≫ (e j).hom =
      (e i).hom ≫ restrictedOverCohomologyMap k F₀ q (D₀.map f) U)
    (he₀ : ∀ i : I, B.ι.app (op i) ≫ e₀.hom =
      (e i).hom ≫ restrictedOverCohomologyMap k F₀ q (c₀.π.app i) U) :
  EtaleComplexCohomologyPresentationData H B
